{'index': 0, 'translation': 'Apple turns 50 this year, and many of its customers are even older than the company itself. To mark the occasion, the company has launched a new support page listing 50 ways to make its devices easier to use, most of which involve accessibility settings.'}

{'index': 1, 'translation': 'The methods cover a wide range, from adjusting text size on the Apple Watch to having your iPhone alert you when the washing machine has finished a cycle…'}

{'index': 2, 'translation': 'Apple says its goal is to make its technology accessible to everyone, including older adults.'}

{'index': 3, 'translation': "At Apple, we believe the best technology should work for everyone — including older adults. That's why our products and services are designed to be inclusive from the start, with built-in features that help you connect, create, and do what you love in whatever way works best for you. As your needs change throughout life, so does the way you interact with the world around you. From making text larger on screen to hearing conversations more clearly in a noisy restaurant, the entire ecosystem of Apple devices, features and services is built to flex and adapt to your needs."}

{'index': 4, 'translation': 'The support page primarily introduces various accessibility features and is divided into ten categories.'}

  • {'index': 5, 'translation': 'Vision: View your screen comfortably'}
  • {'index': 6, 'translation': 'Hearing: Stay connected to conversations, alerts and your surroundings'}
  • {'index': 7, 'translation': 'Mobility: Customise the way you operate and control your device'}
  • {'index': 8, 'translation': 'Speech: Speak in your own way'}
  • {'index': 9, 'translation': 'Cognition: Focus and stay in control'}
  • {'index': 10, 'translation': 'Personalisation: Make it yours'}
  • {'index': 11, 'translation': 'Organisation: Remember what matters'}
  • {'index': 12, 'translation': 'Health: Keep tabs on your wellbeing with useful information'}
  • {'index': 13, 'translation': 'Safety: Enjoy peace of mind'}
  • {'index': 14, 'translation': 'Communication: Stay in touch'}

{'index': 15, 'translation': 'Take the Vision category as an example. It includes options to enlarge text, switch to bold, invert colours, set colour filters, reduce transparency, boost contrast and minimise on-screen motion. Some features, such as Sound Recognition, are little known, but Apple gave them a prominent push when they first launched.'}

{'index': 16, 'translation': "Sound Recognition listens for specific sounds and uses on-device intelligence to notify you when it detects them. It can recognise 15 different sounds, and users can also train their devices to recognise their own name, as well as distinctive electronic sounds in their environment — such as a beeping kitchen appliance, a specific type of alarm or doorbell. On the HomePod, Sound Recognition can also detect smoke or carbon monoxide alarms. Sound Recognition is also supported on CarPlay, where your iPhone will listen for and detect sirens, horns and even a baby's crying. When a specific sound is detected, you'll receive a notification — and when using CarPlay, that notification appears on your car's display."}

{'index': 17, 'translation': "The page is an impressively comprehensive round-up of the accessibility features now spread across Apple's devices. Each section provides standalone guidance for every supported device, and depending on the feature, the coverage can span the iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, Apple TV, Vision Pro and CarPlay."}
